input.model_so_far: Input shaft (axle-input-T, gear-blue-U) meshes with the main shaft's gear-gray-L; the dog-clutch sleeve sits between gear-gray-L and gear-red-P.

new_parts.name: ext-V
new_parts.position: on axle-input-T's free end, sticking out the bottom of the frame as a handle

new_parts.name: ext-W
new_parts.position: on axle-N's free end, sticking out the top-right of the frame as the output

what_each_new_part_touches: ext-V's cross hole locks onto axle-input-T's free end
ext-W's cross hole locks onto axle-N's free end~
where_everything_is_after: ext-V: new, the input handle, sticking out the bottom
ext-W: new, the output handle, sticking out the top-right
everything else: no change -- model complete

why.problem_solved: Finishes both shaft ends as external handles a motor or another model can plug into.
why.why_these_parts: A ridged axle connector gives a longer, grippable stub with a cross hole on its far end, so the shaft can reach past the frame and still take another axle.
why.sets_up_for_later: Nothing further in this 11-step booklet -- this is the last step. ext-V is where you'd turn the gearbox by hand or motor; ext-W is where the selected speed comes out.

review_note: The '2x' callout matches the count directly here (one extension added to each of the two exposed shaft ends in the same picture), unlike the forward-preview '2x' in step 1.
